logic.note: Runs the real compiled arduino-pico firmware on an RP2040 emulator (rp2040js, core 0): GPIO, PWM, ADC, UART, I2C, SPI, PIO, DMA, timers, interrupts and USB serial behave like the chip. Wire and SPI talk to the I2C and SPI parts wired to the board's default bus pins; Serial1/Serial2 bytes travel bit by bit on their TX/RX pins. The boot ROM is Jumper's own implementation of the ROM function table (float and double maths, memory copy, flash erase and program), not Raspberry Pi's ROM code.

timing.note: Instructions are counted at the firmware's clk_sys on a deterministic virtual clock, so delay(), millis() and PWM periods are exact in virtual time. Bus wait states, the flash cache (XIP) and contention are not modelled; ROM routines (float maths, memcpy, flash erase) take typical cycle counts, not exact ones.

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with 50 Ω output resistance and 50 kΩ internal pull-ups. Digital inputs switch at 0.8 V (low) and 2.0 V (high) and keep their last level in between. The 12-bit ADC on GP26-GP29 reads the solved net voltage against an ideal 3.3 V reference; its noise, the RP2040 ADC's non-linearity and its input impedance are ignored.

power.note: 5V (USB VBUS) and 3V3 are stiff sources; per-pin current above 12 mA is flagged. The LDO's limit, brownout and sleep current are not simulated.

emulates: RP2040 core 0 (Cortex-M0+) via rp2040js, at the firmware's clock (125 MHz by default)
Digital I/O with pull-ups, 3.3 V thresholds
12-bit ADC on GP26-GP29 (analogRead, 10-bit by default in arduino-pico)
Serial1/Serial2 on their TX/RX pins at the set baud rate
I2C (Wire) and SPI to the parts on the default bus pins
PIO state machines, DMA, timers and interrupts
doesNotEmulate: Raspberry Pi's own boot ROM code (Jumper implements the same function table natively; transcendental maths may differ in the last bit)
BOOTSEL button, UF2 drag-and-drop upload and the RUN pin
Flash contents across a reset: EEPROM and LittleFS writes are lost on reset
Target (slave) mode of the two-wire bus controller, Wire.begin(address): the board can only be the bus master
Bus electrical detail: the two-wire and serial-peripheral buses carry whole bytes, not clock edges, so clock stretching, rise times and bus capacitance are not modelled
Bus pins other than the board's defaults: Wire.setSDA()/setSCL() and SPI.setRX()/setTX() to other pins do not reach the parts
Frame formats other than 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit on Serial1/Serial2
Floating inputs: an input with nothing driving it reads LOW instead of random noise (the simulator warns about it)
Sleep / dormant modes and their current
The WS2812 RGB LED on GP16 (its data still runs, nothing is drawn)
Underside pads (only the edge pins are modelled as pins)
testOnRealDevice: Anything that uses core 1 (setup1/loop1, multicore FIFO)
Analog readings: the RP2040 ADC is noisy and non-linear near codes 512, 1536, 2560 and 3584
Total current from many pins (50 mA for all GPIOs together)
Every 5 V part: RP2040 pins are not 5 V tolerant; use a level shifter
Upload by BOOTSEL / UF2 and USB enumeration on your computer
